title: 2011 AMC 10A Problem 4
statement: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be the following sums of arithmetic sequences: \[\begin{aligned} X &= 10+12+14+\cdots+100,\\ Y &= 12+14+16+\cdots+102. \end{aligned}\] What is the value of \(Y - X?\)

solutions.text:
Note that the terms \(12\) through \(100\) are common to both sums. When we subtract, all these terms cancel out.

This means that \[ Y - X = 102 - 10 = 92. \]

Thus, A is the correct answer.
hints: Most terms in the two sums cancel
Only the first term of \(X\) and the last term of \(Y\) do not match
